title: Describing a substance: singular adjective
summary: Use a singular partitive adjective to describe a familiar substance.
objectives: Use a singular partitive adjective to describe a familiar substance.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Use a singular partitive adjective to describe a familiar substance.
The substance noun stays in its basic form as the subject. The describing adjective after on has a different job from an adjective placed before a noun.

The examples describe substances, not a particular serving treated as one whole item. The same substance description keeps its partitive adjective under negation; negation alone is not the reason for the case.
keyPoints: When describing a substance as an uncounted substance in this pattern, use a singular partitive adjective after on or ei ole.

steps: When describing a substance as an uncounted substance in this pattern, use a singular partitive adjective after on or ei ole.
Kahvi means “coffee” and works as the noun in its dictionary form used as the subject. kahvi is the dictionary form, with no case ending added.
on means “is / there is / there are” and works as the verb. on comes from olla: the present third-person singular form on.
kuumaa means “hot” and works as the singular partitive adjective describing the substance. Keep kuuma and add -a: kuuma + a = kuumaa.
When describing a substance as an uncounted substance in this pattern, use a singular partitive adjective after on or ei ole.
Maito means “milk” and works as the noun in its dictionary form used as the subject. maito is the dictionary form, with no case ending added.
on means “is / there is / there are” and works as the verb. on comes from olla: the present third-person singular form on.
kylmää means “cold” and works as the singular partitive adjective describing the substance. Keep kylmä and add -ä: kylmä + ä = kylmää.
When describing a substance as an uncounted substance in this pattern, use a singular partitive adjective after on or ei ole.
Keitto means “soup” and works as the noun in its dictionary form used as the subject. keitto is the dictionary form, with no case ending added.
on means “is / there is / there are” and works as the verb. on comes from olla: the present third-person singular form on.
hyvää means “good” and works as the singular partitive adjective describing the substance. Keep hyvä and add -ä: hyvä + ä = hyvää.
When describing a substance as an uncounted substance in this pattern, use a singular partitive adjective after on or ei ole.
Mehu means “juice” and works as the noun in its dictionary form used as the subject. mehu is the dictionary form, with no case ending added.
on means “is / there is / there are” and works as the verb. on comes from olla: the present third-person singular form on.
tuoretta means “fresh” and works as the singular partitive adjective describing the substance. Keep tuore and add -tta: tuore + tta = tuoretta.

commonMistakes: Do not put the substance subject into partitive just because the adjective is partitive.
A description of one countable object follows a different pattern.
